candidates.attacker_control: The action method name is fully attacker-controlled through the URL when DMI is enabled: the method:<payload> request parameter (DefaultActionMapper.METHOD_PREFIX) and/or <action>!<payload>.action (DefaultActionMapper.parseActionName). The value is only stripped of its prefix and otherwise used verbatim.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that DMI is off by default; checked that ParametersInterceptor applies an accepted-pattern whitelist and an excluded-pattern blacklist to parameter names (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/interceptor/ParametersInterceptor.java:267-309, 412-444) so the normal parameter path is hardened; checked that SecurityMemberAccess blocks Object-declared members (getClass), blocks static methods unless enabled, and blocks java.lang/ognl/javax packages (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/ognl/SecurityMemberAccess.java:55-131), which raises the bar but does not sanitize the DMI method expression; checked that struts-default.xml/default.properties do not sanitize method names; checked that DefaultActionMapper.cleanupActionName sanitizes only action names, not method values.
candidates.impact: Remote OGNL expression evaluation on the server; crafted expressions can perform arbitrary method/context manipulation leading to remote code execution, or at minimum invoke unintended action methods, under a DMI-enabled configuration. This is the same class as the later-fixed S2-032/CVE-2016-3081 issue, and this snapshot version (2.3.20.1-SNAPSHOT) falls in the affected 2.3.20-2.3.28 range.
candidates.prerequisites: struts.enable.DynamicMethodInvocation must be true (default is false in core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/default.properties:104-109, but applications enable it, e.g. apps/showcase/src/main/resources/struts.xml sets it true), and the target package must not enforce Strict Method Invocation with an explicit allowed-methods list (default packages do not, so allowedMethods degrades to WILDCARD). The request must be routed through DefaultActionMapper.
candidates.root_cause: DefaultActionMapper stores the raw, unsanitized method: parameter value (and the text after an exclamation mark in the action name) into ActionMapping.method (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/mapper/DefaultActionMapper.java:136-142 and 269-284). DefaultActionProxy.resolveMethod copies it into proxy.method and validates it only with ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/DefaultActionProxy.java:163-192). ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod returns true for any string when allowedMethods holds the default WILDCARD (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/config/entities/ActionConfig.java:137-143, with Builder.embalmTarget adding WILDCARD at lines 346-349), so no validation applies to the method text for ordinary (non-SMI) actions. DefaultActionInvocation.invokeAction then concatenates this attacker-controlled string into an OGNL expression and evaluates it via ognlUtil.getValue(methodName + "()", ...) (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/DefaultActionInvocation.java:410-443), so the method name is parsed and executed by OGNL rather than treated as an identifier. OgnlUtil.getValue performs no expression-character sanity check (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/ognl/OgnlUtil.java:306-312), and OGNL evaluates inner method calls for side effects before the appended final call fails.
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled DMI method name is evaluated as OGNL (OGNL injection / possible RCE when Dynamic Method Invocation is enabled)
candidates.trace: Request URL/parameter -> DefaultActionMapper.handleSpecialParameters/parseActionName sets ActionMapping.method to raw attacker text -> DefaultActionProxy.prepare() -> resolveMethod() copies it -> config.isAllowedMethod(method) returns true (WILDCARD default) -> DefaultActionInvocation.invokeAction() evaluates ognlUtil.getValue(methodName + "()", stack context, action) -> OGNL parses and executes the attacker's expression; inner method calls run before the trailing appended call fails.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed and no exploit payload is provided. I could not verify that a working OGNL payload always survives the appended "()" and the SecurityMemberAccess class/package restrictions in this exact build, and the DMI-enabled prerequisite is not the framework default. I also could not confirm from the snapshot which specific upstream fix a 2.3.20.1 release targeted, so the intended ground-truth issue may be a different one (for example an SMI/wildcard or pattern-checker bypass).
candidates.weakness_type: OGNL expression injection (CWE-917/CWE-94) via unsanitized dynamic method name

coverage_summary: 2866 model-visible source files (binary-like files skipped; no symlink or sensitive-name exclusions). I read the core request pipeline and security controls in depth: DefaultActionMapper, DefaultActionProxy, DefaultActionInvocation, ActionConfig/XmlConfigurationProvider method handling, ParametersInterceptor, CookieInterceptor, the Accepted/Excluded pattern checkers, OgnlUtil/OgnlValueStack/SecurityMemberAccess, struts-default.xml and default.properties, the static content loader, and several result classes. Plugins (rest, json, convention, dojo, embeddedjsp, tiles, spring and others), the apps/ and archetypes/ modules, and view templates were only spot-checked, not exhaustively reviewed.
limitations: No test sources are present in the snapshot, so behavior was inferred from production code only.
No build, runtime, or exploit validation was performed (read-only review only), so all impact statements are source-based.

The specific upstream fix a Struts 2.3.20.1 release addressed could not be confirmed from the snapshot (no changelog or CVE strings), so the candidate is the strongest source-supported issue found rather than a verified ground-truth match.
Large areas (plugins and example apps) were not exhaustively inspected; another injected or real issue could exist there.

rejected_leads.lead: Excluded/accepted regex weaknesses (for example '.' not matching newlines making the class excluded pattern skippable for names like foo newline .class.classLoader).
rejected_leads.reason: In the parameter path the accepted-pattern whitelist rejects names containing newlines or other unsupported characters, and SecurityMemberAccess independently blocks Object-declared members (getClass) and java.lang/ognl/javax packages, so no complete bypass could be evidenced from source alone. CookieInterceptor is only affected when the application configures cookiesName (empty by default), and dangerous prefixes such as '#' are rejected by its accepted pattern.

rejected_leads.lead: XSS/information exposure in DebuggingInterceptor (debug=xml/console/browser writes request/session values into responses).
rejected_leads.reason: Guarded by devMode (struts.devMode=false by default; FilterDispatcher.overrideDevMode is never set from a request in this snapshot), so it is a configuration-dependent hardening gap rather than an unconditionally reachable vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Static resource path traversal and result-location handling in DefaultStaticContentLoader / result classes.
rejected_leads.reason: DefaultStaticContentLoader already checks that the resolved resource URL ends with the built resource path (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/DefaultStaticContentLoader.java:181-199); no traversal could be evidenced.

rejected_leads.lead: PostbackResult writes finalLocation unescaped into HTML (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/PostbackResult.java:96-99).
rejected_leads.reason: finalLocation derives from result configuration, not directly from request input in the default configuration; no attacker-controlled path to the unescaped sink could be established, so this is at most a hardening item.

summary: Snapshot is Apache Struts 2.3.20.1-SNAPSHOT (pom.xml), containing xwork-core, core, plugins and apps. I reviewed the request-handling/OGNL trust boundary: DefaultActionMapper, DefaultActionProxy, DefaultActionInvocation, ParametersInterceptor, CookieInterceptor, the new Accepted/ExcludedPatternsChecker security services, OgnlUtil/SecurityMemberAccess, struts-default.xml/default.properties, the static content loader and several result classes. The default parameter path (ParametersInterceptor plus the accepted/excluded pattern checkers) is consistently hardened, and the static-content loader already contains its path-prefix check. The strongest source-evidenced weakness is the Dynamic Method Invocation path: a method name taken from the URL or the method: parameter is fed unsanitized into OGNL (methodName + "()"), and the only guard (ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod) trivially returns true when the default WILDCARD is present (Strict Method Invocation not configured), yielding OGNL evaluation of attacker-controlled text and side-effecting method calls. One candidate submitted; other leads were rejected as unsupported.
